subject: 🏃 Thursday — 6 mi Progression Run (Wk 3)
html:
Tomorrow: 6 mi Progression Run. Four miles easy at ~9:00 pace, then two miles at threshold by HR (155–162 BPM, cap 165). Pace is the check, HR is the anchor — accept whatever your legs give you at the right heart rate. Polar H10 on.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction, each leg), banded lateral walks (10 each way), glute bridges (10 reps, 2-sec hold at top), plus the PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

The known confounder: Yesterday's heavy session hit 165 lb on both squat and RDL — your legs will feel it. The May 14 progression run showed the same Wed→Thu pattern: threshold miles ran 7:38/7:42 instead of 7:15–7:25, but HR was 159–162 and Z4 time-in-zone was 19:30 — threshold dose fully delivered. Expect pace to be 5–10 sec/mi slower than the flat target at correct HR. That's informational about residual fatigue, not a failed workout.

Focus cue: Stay honest in the easy miles. The first four should feel genuinely conversational — HR under 145, pace floating wherever it lands. The temptation after a rest day from running (no run yesterday) is to push too early. Save the effort for the threshold finish.

Knee status: Three consecutive 1/5 days (Mon–Wed) after the B2B 2/5 reading. Clean trend. If anything whispers in the medial PFJ area during the threshold miles, back off to easy pace immediately — don't push through.

Context: Week 3 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation — 66 days to race day. This is the second progression run in the plan (first was May 14). The May 30 PAL 10K is 9 days out — that's the real calibration race. Friday is stability & power at Cañada, so tomorrow's run is your only run day this week until Saturday's shakeout.

Tonight: Carb-forward dinner — rice bowl, sweet potato, or pasta with fish. Lay out your gear and the H10 strap tonight. Bed by 10, alarm for 5:45.
